allowed_ips_json.description:
AllowedIPsJSON is empty for unrestricted legacy keys. An explicit empty
array denies every source address; entries may be IPs or CIDRs.

request_quota.description:
RequestQuota is the monthly logical request budget for this key
(0 = unlimited). Provider and upstream retries reuse the reservation.

rotated_to_key_id.description:
RotatedToKeyID is the successor created by a rotation (doc/301 GW-4). It is
also the rotation's idempotency guard: a key that already has a successor
cannot be rotated again, so a double click cannot produce two live secrets.
The retired key keeps working until `ExpiredAt` — that window *is* the grace
period, so there is no second clock to disagree with the expiry check.

token_quota.description:
TokenQuota is the monthly token budget for this key (0 = unlimited). It
is the spending-control input for gateway quota preauthorization.

canvas_category.description:
CanvasCategory is copied from the live RAGFlow canvas for API views.
RAGFlow remains authoritative and the ownership shadow does not store it.

retrieval_pushdown.description:
RetrievalPushdownJSON records the retrieval-layer metadata_condition
pushdown evidence (doc/123 §7): {"status":"applied|bypassed|absent",
"condition":{...}}. absent = scenario has no pushdown channel.

budget_tokens.description:
BudgetTokens is the *frozen* cap the run was started with (0 = mechanical
layer only). A later settings change must not rewrite what this run could
afford, or the `budget_exhausted` status would become unexplainable.

method_version.description:
MethodVersion names the judgement rules the run used. A later rule change
must not silently reinterpret a past week's counters.

scenario_template_id.description:
ScenarioTemplateID/Version record which wizard template produced this
assistant. Bare POST /chats stays possible (API clients) but then these
stay empty and the assistant is not trial-run eligible.

index.description:
Index is the zero-based position of this citation within the turn's
reference list, so the UI can map answer-side [n] markers to the drawer
without relying on opaque chunk ids (P2 citation experience).

positions.description:
Positions preserves the engine-provided in-document locator keys
(positions/bbox/page/offset/paragraph/line_*...) verbatim as JSON so the
forward UI can highlight the cited span inside the source document.

adapter_kind.description:
AdapterKind records who executes the source scan. Native keeps the whole
business loop inside X; ragflow is reserved for the Tier-B adapter and is
currently rejected at create/update time.

created_by.description:
CreatedBy is the user who submitted the binding (approval requester when
governed). It is immutable after creation.

credential_version.description:
CredentialVersion increments on every successful rotation so run/audit
evidence can be tied to the credential generation in use.

enabled.description:
Enabled is the explicit scheduling switch (doc/225 §5.1). Status is the
runtime health signal (idle|degraded|disabled); keeping both avoids
overloading a health field with operator intent. The column default is
false (fail-closed for raw inserts); CreateConnector explicitly opts in,
because GORM replaces zero values with a true default and would silently
re-enable a connector created with enabled=false.

external_connector_id.description:
ExternalConnectorID is the remote connector id for a RAGFlow-backed
adapter. Empty for native bindings.

source_ownership_key.description:
SourceOwnershipKey is the canonical "one logical source, one connector"
identity (tenant + provider + target dataset + source target) and backs a
unique index. Credentials are deliberately excluded so rotation never
changes identity (doc/227 C2.3).

external_run_id.description:
ExternalRunID is the remote run id for a RAGFlow-backed adapter, kept on
the X run row so operators never have to open the engine to explain a run.

triggered_by.description:
TriggeredBy is the acting user for manual runs and "system" for scheduled
runs, so the run row is self-describing without joining audit logs.

authority.description: Authority is the 权威度 等级分 (0-100).

dataset_id.description:
DatasetID is the X-side dataset link id; DocumentID is the RAGFlow
document id (source of truth for downstream retrieval filtering).

artifact_version.description:
ArtifactVersion is allocated inside the revision row lock; re-exporting the
same revision always takes MAX+1 and never revives an expired row (292 D3).

created_by.description: Soft-delete trail for report artifacts; answering exports leave them empty.

day.description:
Day is the reconciled UTC date ("2006-01-02"). It is the idempotency guard
together with the tenant: a replayed daily job cannot reconcile the same day
twice and double-count its findings.

quota_expected_tokens.description:
QuotaExpectedTokens is the sum of settled reservations and
QuotaActualTokens the sum of the keys' used balances, over the buckets this
run examined. Both raw numbers, so a reader can redo the subtraction.

usage_metered_requests.description:
UsageMeteredRequests / UsageBilledRequests are the two sides of the third
ledger pair. Stored even when they agree: "0 vs 0" and "40 vs 40" are different
statements about the day, and only one of them means requests happened.

abstain_rate_warn.description:
Operator levers (config.knowledge_ops): thresholds the data engineer can
tune. *RateWarn/Floor are echoed verbatim so the board renders the bar;
*AboveWarn/*BelowBaseline/*BelowFloor flag when the observed value crosses
the bar (ABS too high, citation rate too low, similarity too low).

avg_top_similarity.description:
AvgTopSimilarity is the mean top retrieval similarity across completed
turns that produced at least one measurable reference (P2 observability).

attempts.description:
Attempts counts write attempts across the first try and every recovery
pass, so "kept failing" and "failed once, recovered" read differently.

date.description:
Date is the metering day, fixed when the intent is prepared: a recovery at
00:05 must book the request to the day it was served, not to today.

tokens_out.description:
TokensOut and Requests are stored so a replay reproduces the original
aggregate increment exactly (Requests is 1 per request today).

current_pin_id.description:
CurrentPinID/Version are an explicit pointer to an immutable enterprise
runtime pin. Legacy routes may leave both empty.

version_preflight_observed.description:
VersionPreflight* (T6.3, doc/223 T6 / doc/224 §2.4 / v0.3.0 version-line
merge): the capability version-band preflight observed at release time.
Production CreateRelease fails closed when a confident band violation is
detected (engine newer than the verified band, or unparseable). The
probe result is recorded on the release row as audit evidence.

cleanup_hold_until.description:
CleanupHoldUntil is the recovery window after a soft delete. It never
extends ExpiresAt (doc/288 §7.6).

expires_at.description:
ExpiresAt is the frozen report-class TTL (doc/288 §7.6): written once at
creation from the live policy, read verbatim by the janitor.

budget_policy.description:
ReportBudgetPolicy is `enforce` (refuse a call that would cross the envelope)
or `observe` (record it and keep going). Empty reads as `enforce` so every row
written before this column existed keeps its behaviour.

finalized_at.description:
FinalizedAt non-null means the terminal write already happened; it is the
idempotency criterion of finalize (doc/288 §8.2).

pending_reconcile_tokens.description:
PendingReconcileTokens keeps unconfirmable reservations visible instead of
reporting them as 0 (292 D7).

reserved_tokens.description:
ReservedTokens is the envelope frozen at creation. `ReportBudgetPolicy` says
whether it is a limit or a measurement; both are frozen here so a tenant-wide
switch flipped mid-run cannot change a job that is already spending (doc/296
§2.2). An extension approved through governance raises this number and never
touches `rgx_report_charge`: the ledger records what was spent, this column
records what was allowed.

assurance_ack_json.description:
AssuranceAckJSON records the explicit "export anyway" acknowledgement: who,
when, and what they were shown. Renamed from the first draft's
`publish_ack_json`, which read as a *publish* confirmation (doc/301 §6.2).

assurance_run_id.description:
GapJSON is written by finalize together with the terminal state; the
banner, the job.partial payload and the artifact disclosure only read it.
AssuranceRunID / AssuranceStatus / AssuranceSummaryJSON / AssuranceAckJSON
are a *rebuildable projection* of the latest assurance run (doc/301 §6.2).
They may be overwritten by a new run, so code must never answer "was this
revision assured when it was published" from them — the immutable answer is
an `rgx_report_assurance_run` row plus `assurance_ack_json`.

datasets_json.description:
DatasetsJSON is the knowledge binding frozen at creation (doc/288 §13):
`[{dataset_id, engine_dataset_id, role}]`. It is written before the outline
step because that step is the first one that needs to retrieve, and it is
the only durable record of "which datasets may this report cite" — the
execution snapshot is written *after* it and reads this column.

published_at.description:
No clock of its own: a revision lives and dies with its report (doc/288
§7.2 column list). The evidence-safe clock belongs to the snapshot.

research_depth.description:
ResearchDepth freezes R18's planning switch (doc/295 §2.2). `standard` is the
P0/P1 behaviour (one retrieval per section); `deep` lets the runner plan
sub-queries before writing. It lives on the revision, not the report, because
a deep run and a standard rerun of the same report are different conditions.

reuse_plan_json.description:
ReusePlanJSON freezes R14's local carry-over request (doc/288 §9.8): the base
revision's section ords this revision asked to inherit. It is written once at
creation and never mutated, so an operator reading a surprising report can
tell "the user asked for reuse" from "the writer produced the same text".

trigger.description:
Trigger and ScheduleID record who asked for this revision (doc/295 §2.4).
`manual` is every revision a human asked for — creation, regeneration, and the
retry path's re-drafting — so an empty value would be ambiguous rather than
"the old shape"; the migration backfills `manual`.

evidence_preview_json.description:
EvidencePreviewJSON is the outline-time evidence盘面 (doc/288 §9.6): how many
chunks this section's query hit, the main source documents, and whether that
is thin against `min_evidence`. It is frozen when the outline is written, in
the same transaction, so the reviewer's confirmation is recorded next to the
evidence they saw. Advisory only — it is never a sufficiency verdict, which
is why `insufficient` can be null ("did not look").

gap_reason.description:
GapReason is why the section ended without content, from the closed set
`failed | skipped | budget_exhausted` (doc/288 §7.8 `gap_json.reason`). It is
written by the runner that made the decision because the reason cannot be
reconstructed afterwards: `quality_status='failed'` is set both when the
budget bail-out skipped the section and when the model actually failed, and
the two are different promises to the reader ("buy more budget" vs "fix the
source"). Empty on a row that succeeded.

location_hints_json.description:
LocationHintsJSON is R17: compilation artifacts (page index / wiki / tree)
that help a reader find the source page. They are *navigation*, never
evidence — nothing here reaches `rgx_report_citation`, the evidence snapshot
or the claim support check (doc/295 A54). Frozen at outline time so the
reader sees the same locator the author did.

pool_hit_chunks.description:
ResearchPlanJSON is R18: the planner's sub-queries, how many chunks each
returned, and which fallback (if any) replaced the plan. Written with
`prompt_hash` at BeginReportSection because it describes that prompt's inputs.
PoolHitChunks / PoolInsufficient / PoolCandidateCount are the *writing-time*
retrieval pool of this section (doc/301 §5.8 item 1), the counterpart of the
outline-time `evidence_preview_json`. All three are nullable on purpose:
`NULL` means "this revision did not record it", which is not the same answer
as `0` (= the pool returned nothing) — the same discipline as
`evidence_preview_json.insufficient`.

requires_evidence.description:
No column default on purpose: gorm omits a zero-valued field that declares
one, so `false` would silently be stored as the default (`true`) and a
template saying "this section needs no evidence" could never take effect.

sync_state.description:
SyncState is derived from lifecycle, governance, and baseline evidence;
it is intentionally not persisted.

baseline_key.description:
Baseline provenance (doc/276 §7.1, migration 165). A tenant row that was
explicitly forked from a platform baseline records which baseline key and
version it derives from; LineageState keeps `copy` + empty BaselineKey
from meaning "same-tenant copy" and "unknown baseline" at once.

payload_schema.description:
Historical immutability (doc/276 §7.7 / R7). Existing rows keep their
payload verbatim and are stamped `v2/authored`; a v3 payload is stored as
`v3/authored`. A v2 payload re-materialized during a migration is
`v2/legacy_reconstructed` and may never be sold as "identical to history",
because the frozen preset snapshot captures the migration-time values.

scenario_template_id.description:
Template provenance (doc/276 §7.5, migration 166). Chat keeps the same pair
in rgx_chat_shadow; search apps and agents get it here so all three forms
can be traced back to the template version they were instantiated from.

sync_state.description: SyncState is service-derived synchronization evidence for UI use.

idempotency_key.description:
Unified instantiation state machine (doc/276 §7.5 / R24). The idempotency
key comes from the `Idempotency-Key` header only, and the partial unique
index on (tenant_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key <> '' is what
actually makes instantiation idempotent — upstream probing is best-effort.

name_key.description:
NameKey records the requested instance name so instantiation replays can
find the same projection (doc/124 §2.2); it is not the assistant name.

upstream_refs.description:
UpstreamRefs keeps the ids of resources already created in the engine so a
retry can skip them; it is never used to rewrite local state.

auto_route_mode.description:
AutoRouteMode is the tenant-level kill switch and gradual rollout mode.
The system policy remains an outer boundary and can never be bypassed.

role.description:
Role is a denormalized read-only primary/default-role marker derived from
rgx_user_role (the authoritative RBAC source). It is kept consistent by
SetUserPrimaryRole and is used for display/JWT/legacy fallback only.

cred_fields.description:
CredFields describes the credential form (sealed KV map). S3 needs two
values (access_key_id/access_secret) and WebDAV two (username/password),
so the wizard cannot be driven by a single field name.

type.description:
Type discriminates canvas rows on v1.0.0+: the /agents list also surfaces
compilation template groups ("type":"compilation_template_group"), which are
a different resource and must not be synced as runnable agents.

from.description: From/To are the before/after spellings for the fixed value.

kind.description: Kind is component_name | node_id | node_link | prompt_param | message_content.

label.description: Label is the canvas label of that node, when one was available.

message.description: Message is a ready-to-display sentence (English; the UI localises by Kind).

node_id.description: NodeID is the node the fix applies to (post-rename id for node_id fixes).

update_time.description:
UpdateTime is the engine's millisecond epoch (the engine stores ms, not
seconds). Consumers must not multiply it by 1000.

chunk_id.description:
RAGFlow 1.0 rc2 returns the native chunk envelope with chunk_id /
content_with_weight instead of the legacy id / content fields. Keep
both shapes so the engine boundary remains version tolerant.

unclassifiedVersion.description:
UnclassifiedVersion counts endpoints that declare neither MinVersion
nor MaxVerified - the T6.3 re-verification backlog the version preflight
cannot yet gate (currently empty: every entry is classified to 1.0.0).

capability.description: Capability names the related Capability Matrix entry ("*" = family-wide).

finding.description: Finding summarises the delta for the 对账表 and the upgrade preflight.

status.description: Status anchors the row per the enum above.

version.description: Version is the release the delta was observed against.

pushdown_enabled.description:
PushdownEnabled gates retrieval metadata pushdown for this dataset
(doc/123 §3): when true, the dataset's sensitivity is synced to
RAGFlow meta_fields and participates in metadata_condition filtering.

compilation_templates.description:
Compilation templates are what the dataflow Compiler node must name: the
engine resolves one of these ids at run time and rejects the node without
it, so a free-text id was an unbuildable field.

vision_models.description:
VisionModels are the engine's image2text/ocr models: the only values the
dataflow Parser node accepts for a model-based `parse_method` (or for
`vlm.llm_id` when vision enhancement is on).

code.description: Code is a stable identifier the UI localises (agents.validation.<code>).

message.description: Message is a ready-to-read English sentence for CLI/API consumers.

node_label.description: NodeLabel is the canvas label, which is what the author actually saw.

params.description: Params carries the interpolation values for the localised message.

unlabelled_answered.description: UnlabelledAnswered is the population the feedback-derived rates could not see.

abstain_rate.description: Rates. nil means "no denominator": 0/0 is unknown, never 0%.

citations_missing.description:
Raw counts behind every rate, so the reader can print the denominator next to it
instead of trusting a percentage. `CitationMissing` has no rate of its own beyond
`CitationMissingRate` but travels anyway: the board renders "n/m".

similarity_samples.description:
Retrieval similarity. `SimilaritySamples` counts turns with a measurable value
(> 0); when it is 0 both quantiles are nil rather than 0.

assurance_review_transport.description:
ReviewTransport is `provider_direct` or `engine_chat`: it records *how* the
review question will be asked, because on this engine the answer does not
say which model produced it (doc/304 E125/E127). A run whose transport is
`engine_chat` reports `independence=unknown` by construction.

assurance_review_transport_reason.description:
ReviewTransportReason says *why* that route was chosen, in the operator's
words: "the reference names no instance", "model X is not registered on
instance Y", … Without it a run that silently fell back to the engine looks
exactly like a run that was never meant to go direct, and the operator's only
recourse is to guess which of the four gates refused (doc/304 E129).

source.description:
Source names the evidence origin so the UI never shows a bare badge
without provenance (doc/276 §6.5 rule 4).

status.description: Status is the highest state proven; empty means "not supported".

chunk_method.description:
ChunkMethod is the target parse profile for `apply_parse_profile`. The
server decides it from parse_intent; the wizard must not re-derive it
from prose (it used to fall back to `naive` and repair towards the wrong
method, doc/285 §4).

endpoint.description:
Endpoint is the machine-readable exec path for actions that have one
(doc/282 §6). Only genuinely executable repairs carry a hint; advisory
actions leave it empty rather than promising a fake channel.

requires_reparse.description:
RequiresReparse mirrors the 40915 precondition on the write channel: the
dataset already has parsed documents, so applying the profile re-parses
them and the operator has to confirm that explicitly. Computed here so
the rule exists once, not twice.

created.description:
Created is false when the request was a replay of an identical fork and the
already-committed clone was returned instead (double-click safe).

template.description: Template is the workspace's new fork row.

observation_window_seconds.description:
NOTE: validator's bare `gt` (no param) panics on bind (asInt("") in
validator v10.30), which made the recovery-approval HTTP endpoint 500 on
every request (caught by the M204 live duty drill); `gt=0` is required.

concurrency.description:
Concurrency is present only when the run was accepted but not started: the
workspace already had `limit` runs executing (doc/297 §3). The job is
`queued`, the envelope is frozen, and the reconcile sweep arms it as soon as a
slot frees — so the client is told "accepted, waiting behind N runs" instead of
inventing a status of its own or being told nothing at all.

It is omitted otherwise rather than filled in: a number that is already
changing when the client reads it is worse than no number.

document_count.description:
DocumentCount/ParsedCount let the repair UI say how much work a re-parse
costs ("3 of 5 documents already parsed") instead of a blind warning.

pushdown_enabled.description:
PushdownEnabled gates retrieval metadata pushdown for this dataset
(doc/123 §3): when true, the dataset's sensitivity is synced to
RAGFlow meta_fields and participates in metadata_condition filtering.

supported.description: capability gate: type settable on this build

authority.description: Authority is the 权威度 等级分 (0-100, default 50).

expires_at.description: ExpiresAt optionally disables the annotation after a time.

level.description: Level is the 密级 (internal / confidential / top_secret).

reason.description: Reason is an optional human-readable justification (audit trail).

source.description:
Source records the annotation channel (manual/approval/auto). Empty is
normalized to manual; approval records are stamped automatically.

status.description: Status is the 发布状态 (draft / published, default published).

window.description:
Window names what the counts are taken over, because "0 unsettled" without a
denominator can mean "nothing owed" or "nothing looked at".

dormant.description: 命中扩展词条（暂不可投影）

manual_override.description: 已存在人工/审批标注，auto 不覆盖

matched.description: 至少命中一个可投影 schema 的文档数

quality_skipped.description: 抽取质量未达门槛被拦

schema_used.description: 实际使用的生效 schema 数

sync_failed.description: 回填 RAGFlow 元数据失败（降级计数）

written.description: 写入/更新 auto 标注数

conflict.description:
Conflict records the deterministic Memory/Knowledge conflict-downgrade
evaluation (doc 137 §6.3 #8). Nil only for legacy call sites.

abstain_reason.description:
AbstainReason is `answerability_json.abstain_reason` projected into a column
so the board can *filter* on it (doc/301 T12/QA-1). A JSON text column cannot
be filtered portably across sqlite and postgres, and filtering after the page
is fetched would make the total wrong rather than merely slow. One writer
(`attachAnswerabilityClaim`) sets both, so the projection cannot disagree with
the JSON it came from; "" means the field predates the claim or the claim was
never evaluated — the UI shows that as "not recorded", never as "answerable".

answerability_json.description:
AnswerabilityJSON is the per-turn honesty claim (report §13.2 P0-B):
{answerable, confidence, source, abstain_reason, citation_count, distinct_docs}.
It annotates the turn without rewriting the engine answer.

citation_audit_status.description:
Citation audit state (doc/301 §5.10 QA-2 / T19). The weekly sample writes
its disposition back here so the existing badcase queue can filter on it —
without a second queue table and without rewriting any other field of the
turn. Both strings stay "" until the turn is sampled, which is what
"never audited" looks like; `skipped` is a different value on purpose.

review_status.description: Review state closes the loop from badcase detection to a disposition.

top_similarity.description:
TopSimilarity is the highest retrieval similarity observed for the turn
(engine reference similarity key); 0 means no measurable reference
(P2 operations observability).

acknowledge_shared_impact.description:
AcknowledgeSharedImpact is the explicit confirmation doc/276 §7.4 requires
when other applications already retrieve from this dataset.

endpoint_coverage.description:
EndpointCoverage summarizes the provider endpoint stability registry
(doc/121 B2): how many upstream endpoints RAGFlow-X depends on are
documented in the official API reference versus learned from source and
therefore gated by the internal-endpoint live contract drill.

version_gap_count.description:
VersionGapCount is the count of endpoints still lacking a version band
(T6.2 backlog; 0 after T6.2 classified every endpoint).

version_issues.description:
VersionIssues are the capability-level 版本×能力×契约 observations (223
T6 / 224 §2.4 T6.1), exported so the upgrade reviewer sees the known
cross-version deltas on the Capability Matrix panel.

version_issues_summary.description: VersionSummary rolls up the observation states for the preflight review.

research_depth.description:
ResearchDepth is optional on a rerun: empty inherits the base revision's
depth. Changing it is allowed because the rerun writes a *new* revision, and
§7.4 already treats "same report, different conditions" as a new version.

can_manage.description:
CanManage is true when this caller may change the policy: the owner, or a
platform administrator with `manage` (the same union the write enforces).

is_owner.description:
IsOwner tells the UI whether the share editor is offered. It is not a
permission decision — the write route re-checks it — it is what stops a
reader from being handed a form that will only answer "not found".

release_eligibility.description:
ReleaseEligibility is `pending` until the run ends; after that it is the
single verdict of `reportAssuranceEligibility`.

replayed.description:
Replayed marks a response answered from the idempotency key rather than a
fresh run. A client that retries must be able to tell "your click created
this" from "someone's click created this earlier".

already_requested.description:
AlreadyRequested marks a repeated cancel. It is `false` for a terminal job,
which is refused with 44104 instead: "already finished" must not read as
"your cancel worked".

access.description:
Access is the sharing state (doc/296 §2.1): the policy, whether this caller
may edit it, and the named grantees with their names resolved. It rides on the
detail read instead of a `GET /reports/:id/access` route because a reader that
may open the report can always see how it is shared, and a second route would
be a second place to get the predicate wrong.

artifacts.description:
Artifacts is the delivered-file history of this revision, newest version
first (A11: "跨会话/刷新可见可下载").

It belongs in the read aggregate, not only in the POST that minted it: an
export list that lives in a component's memory disappears on refresh, which
would make yesterday's delivery un-findable while the file itself still sits
on disk. `downloadable` is derived server-side by the same
`reportArtifactDownloadable` the download endpoint uses, so the button state
and the endpoint cannot disagree.

budget.description:
Budget is the spend side of the *live* run (doc/296 §2.2). Nil means there is
nothing to extend: no job, or a job that already finalized. It rides on the
detail read because the extension card has to state the current envelope before
it can ask for more — a client that guessed it would either over-ask (refused)
or under-ask (a second approval round for a number it could have named).

evidence_expired_at.description:
EvidenceExpiredAt is the earliest snapshot clock of this revision, so a client
can say *when* verification stopped rather than just that it did. Nil when no
citations exist.

evidence_verifiable.description:
EvidenceVerifiable answers "can this report's citations still be re-checked?"
(doc/288 §7.6 / A43). It is false once any cited snapshot has been purged or
has passed its own clock — the body and the recorded judgement stay readable,
and the UI must say so instead of quietly offering a citation that opens
nothing. A report with no citations is verifiable: nothing was lost.

metrics.description:
Metrics is `metrics_json` decoded, so the reader can show what the revision's
own quality pass concluded without re-parsing an escaped string. R16's claim
support ratio and cross-section consistency issues live here (doc/288 §9.1 L3).
Nil means the revision never finalized: "not measured yet" is not "all good".

event_seq.description:
EventSeq is the resume cursor. It is the same number the event allocator
reads, so `after=event_seq` can neither skip an event nor replay a duplicate.

gaps.description:
Gaps is `gap_json` as an array; empty (never null) until finalize writes it,
so a UI can map over it without a null check.

cleanup_hold_until.description:
CleanupHoldUntil is the recovery window after a soft delete. It never
extends ExpiresAt (doc/288 §7.6).

expires_at.description:
ExpiresAt is the frozen report-class TTL (doc/288 §7.6): written once at
creation from the live policy, read verbatim by the janitor.

revision.description:
Revision is the number of the current revision (0 when the report has no
revision row left — the retention purge removes both, so this is a
transient shape, not a state to render as a fact).

date.description:
Date is the bucket start in UTC: `2026-11-18` for a day, the Monday of the
week (`2026-11-16`) for a week. A start date is a stable key and cannot be
misread as a label; presentation decides how to print it.

degraded_revisions.description:
DegradedRevisions counts revisions whose stored `quality_flag=degraded`
(citation coverage below the floor, §14.2). It is a count, not a ratio, so a
single flagged revision is visible on a quiet day.

locator_assisted_sections.description:
LocatorAssistedSections / WithCitationSections are the pooled numerator and
denominator of `locator_assisted_section_rate` (doc/301 T10). They are summed
across revisions rather than averaged: a 3-section report and a 30-section one
do not carry the same evidence, and pooling keeps the ratio's denominator
visible next to it.

metrics_missing.description:
MetricsMissing counts terminal revisions whose `metrics_json` could not be
read. They are counted, never silently dropped: a trend that hides the rows it
could not parse reports a cleaner workspace than the one that exists.

quality_judged.description:
QualityJudged / QualityPassed / QualityNeedsReview / QualityNotChecked are the
§14.2 gate counts, summed from the stored per-revision metrics.

research_degraded_sections.description:
ResearchDegradedSections / ResearchPlannedSections are pooled counts from the
per-revision metrics (doc/301 §5.8 item 2). They are counts, never a ratio: the
only decision §5.8 item 3 authorises is "is this common enough to fund planning
v2", and a percentage without its denominator cannot answer it on a quiet week.

structure_completeness.description:
StructureCompleteness averages §14.1's structural ratio over delivered
revisions; CitationCoverage likewise.

degraded_revisions.description:
DegradedRevisions counts revisions whose stored `quality_flag=degraded`
(citation coverage below the floor, §14.2). It is a count, not a ratio, so a
single flagged revision is visible on a quiet day.

from.description:
From is inclusive, To exclusive, both UTC — the same half-open window the
query used, so a caller can page forward without re-deriving it.

truncated.description:
Truncated is true when the window held more terminal revisions than the read
cap. The numbers then describe the newest `Revisions` rows and say so, instead
of quietly averaging a subset.

budget_policy.description:
The two governance switches of the report surface (doc/296 §2.2/§2.3). They
live on this payload because they are the same kind of decision as the clocks:
a tenant-wide answer an operator writes once. Splitting them into a second
endpoint would give the workspace two places to look for "what does this tenant
allow", and two chances for one of them to be stale.

overridden.description: Overridden flags name the fields the tenant pins.

system_report_days.description:
SystemReportDays..SystemCleanupHoldDays are the inherited values, so a client
can render "30 (system 90)" without a second request.

document_label.description:
DocumentLabel is the human name, resolved from this revision's own citation
rows when the same document is cited somewhere else. Empty when the document is
not cited anywhere in the report — a label we cannot derive is left out instead
of being re-read from the live index, which could have been renamed or deleted
since (the same rule the citation appendix follows).

pool_rank.description:
PoolRank is the retrieval order the candidate ranked at, which is the only
signal that makes "the runner-up source contradicted the report" readable.

finding_ids.description:
FindingID lets the claim row open the matching finding without a join on the
client, which would need the same "which finding is about this claim" rule
this function already implements.

matched_snapshot_id.description:
SnapshotID is what the UI highlights inside; `MatchedText` alone cannot point
at a document.

not_required_share.description:
NotRequiredShare is nullable: an empty revision has no share, and printing
0.000 would read as "no claims were exempt" (§4.3).

evidence_status.description:
EvidenceStatus is the section-level roll-up the report already stores; it is
echoed rather than recomputed so the workbench and the document agree.

next_claim_cursor.description:
ClaimCursor is the cursor of the last claim in this section, used when a
single section is itself too long to return whole.

pool_hit_chunks.description:
PoolHitChunks / PoolInsufficient / PoolCandidateCount are the *writing-time*
pool (doc/301 §5.8 item 1), copied from the section row. They are pointers
because `NULL` means "this revision never recorded it" and `0` means "the pool
was empty": a reviewer deciding whether a weak claim is the writer's fault or
the corpus's needs that distinction, and a zeroed field would erase it.

research_planning.description:
ResearchPlanning is the frozen plan state (`standard` / `planned` /
`fallback_*`). §5.8 item 2 shows the degradation where the reviewer already
looks, instead of leaving it in a JSON blob only the export renders.

acknowledgeable.description:
Acknowledgeable marks a revision whose conflicts are known and disclosed:
exporting it needs an explicit `acknowledge_assurance` (§7.2). It is computed
server-side so the checkbox and the 44121 refusal cannot disagree.

candidate_count.description:
CandidateCount is how many uncited candidates were frozen for this revision. It
is a count on purpose: candidate *content* needs a second check against the
caller's current dataset permission, and v0.7.0 exposes the number without the
text (§5.3.1 ACL 读).

candidates.description:
Candidates are the frozen pool of the sections in this response, owner only.
They never carry a chunk id or a score: a candidate is not evidence, and the
moment it has an identifier a renderer will sort it next to a citation (§5.3.1).

candidates_truncated.description:
CandidatesTruncated says the pool was longer than the projection cap, so the
panel prints "前 N 条" instead of implying it showed the whole pool.

candidates_visible.description:
CandidatesVisible states *why* `candidates` is empty (doc/301 §9 反证候选面板):
the report owner sees the frozen excerpts, a share grantee sees the count and the
sentence "另有 N 条未引用候选参与对照". It is a field rather than an inference so
the panel cannot read "retention purged them" and "not your content" as the same
thing.

findings.description: Findings are the open/acknowledged problems, newest severity first.

release_eligibility.description:
Eligibility and Basis are repeated on the top level because they are the two
fields the release banner reads. `Basis` is the list of failed conditions, so
the banner can say *why* a revision is not tier_1 instead of only that it is
not (§4.2).

requested_policy.description:
RequestedPolicy is what the run was allowed to aim at; `required` here with
`eligibility=tier_1` is the honest v0.7.0 combination (§5.5).

scan_scope.description:
ScanScope is the frozen contrast scope of this revision: `cited_only` or
`cited+candidate:K` (doc/301 §5.3.1). It is *required* disclosure — without it
"no conflicts found" reads as "cross-document contrast was performed and found
nothing", which is a much stronger claim than the run made.

truncated.description:
Truncated states which caps were hit, so a client that ignores cursors at
least knows it is looking at a partial answer instead of a complete one.

is_current.description:
IsCurrent is the report's own pointer, not "the newest row". A regenerate that
is still running leaves the pointer on the published base, and a history list
that marks the attempt as current would tell the reader their published report
is the draft that has not finished (the R13/§7.10 defect class).

evidence_preview.description:
EvidencePreview is the outline-time evidence盘面 (doc/288 §9.6), decoded for
the confirmation screen. Nil means nothing was frozen — render 未评估, never
"充足".

location_hints.description:
LocationHints are R17's compiled-artifact locators as display lines, so the
workspace can show the same 「定位线索（非证据）」 line the reader and the three
exports show. They are navigation only: nothing here may be counted as
evidence, and the projection's score/excerpt/chunk id is deliberately absent
(doc/295 §2.1).

claims.description:
Claims are the structured claims of this section (R11 / doc/288 §9.2). They ride
on the section read rather than a route of their own: a claim has no meaning
apart from the paragraph it came from, and a separate collection would need its
own access rule, its own pagination and its own way of being wrong.

location_hints.description:
LocationHints are R17's locators, already rendered as display lines such as
「页面索引：差旅报销制度」. The client prints them under the explicit
「定位线索（非证据）」 label; they are never mixed into the citation list, and the
server sends no chunk ids or scores with them (doc/295 §2.1).

requires_evidence.description:
RequiresEvidence lets the reader explain an empty body ("这一节本来不要求证据"),
instead of leaving the reader to guess why a section is blank.

research_plan.description:
ResearchPlan is R18's disclosure: `nil` for a standard section, and otherwise
the depth, the planning state and how much the extra queries added.

auto_confirm_allowed_roles.description:
AutoConfirmAllowedRoles stays empty in P0-A: turning the outline
confirmation off is a permission on the report owner, not a template
default (292 D2).

output_formats.description:
OutputFormats is the closed set of formats a template *advertises*: docx, md,
pdf, html and xlsx. A template that omits one simply does not advertise it —
this list is a declaration, not an authorization gate: the export endpoint
accepts every format in `validReportExportFormat` for any published revision,
because the rendering contract is the frozen document, not the template's list
(the two lists are therefore deliberately separate, and the report delivery
subset lives in one place on each side: `validReportExportFormat` in Go,
`REPORT_EXPORT_FORMATS` in `report-contract.ts`).

pdf became legal in P0-B, html and xlsx with the fourth-format slice. The three
seeded templates still advertise docx/md/pdf: widening a *stored* payload would
mint a template version every workspace forks from, and a format nobody asked
for is not a reason to change what an already-published report was written
for.

scan_top_k.description:
ScanTopK is how many *uncited* chunks per section are frozen as conflict
candidates at generation time (doc/301 §5.3.1 / §7.6). It is additive on
purpose: an older payload has no key, reads as 0, and inherits the tenant
setting. 0 means "keep none" — widening the retained uncited pool is opt-in,
never a default, because those chunks are content the report did not choose
to cite.

depends_on.description:
DependsOn orders the outline: a section may only be written after the
sections it depends on, which is what makes "先结论后依据" enforceable
instead of a prompt suggestion.

prompt.description:
Prompt is the section-specific instruction. It is a *question shape*, not
an answer, so the same template can serve any knowledge base.

requires_evidence.description:
RequiresEvidence marks sections whose claims must carry citations. At
least one section must require evidence, otherwise the report reduces to
an opinion piece with a compliance cover page.

editable.description:
Editable is true only for a workspace row that is not retired: the platform
baseline ships with the release, and a retired version has no next version
to edit into (publishing under the key still works and mints a new one).

source.description:
Source is `platform` or `workspace` (R19): the UI must be able to say why
a template cannot be edited here rather than offering a button that 400s.

tenant_id.description:
TenantID is the owner of this row: the platform tenant for the baseline, or
the workspace that forked it.

versions.description:
Versions is how many versions of this key the caller can see, and only the
list fills it in; 0 means "not counted" (a single-row answer from publish or
retire). The list itself is one row per key, so without this field the UI
could only ever print "1 version" — a label that would be wrong the moment
anyone edits a template (live 2026-11-19: v2 was displayed as "共 1 个版本").

name.description:
Name is the pack's display name for the dataset (doc/276 §6.4). It is
presentation only: binding still resolves through Suggestions.

required.description:
Required and CreateIfMissing drive the wizard's dataset step: a required
dataset that is missing blocks instantiation unless the caller opts into
creating it (doc/276 §7.5).

baseline_key.description:
Baseline provenance (doc/276 §7.1). `ID` is the platform baseline id when
the workspace has not forked the template; OverridesBaseline=true means
the workspace row shadows the baseline and BaselineUpdateAvailable tells
the UI to offer a re-fork.

eval_gate.description:
EvalGate explains why publish is unavailable for a pack that requires
evaluation evidence (doc/276 §9). Zero value = the pack does not require
it, so the wizard keeps publish enabled.

knowledge.description:
Knowledge is the optional 2.0 knowledge contract (doc/276 §7.2): the
wizard creates datasets with these parse intents and renders the
capability panel from these requirements.

prompt.description:
Prompt and Parameters are the server-resolved instantiation defaults
(doc/228 T7.0 single source of truth). The wizard must render these, not
its own preset table, and must not send them back as overrides.

renderable_app_types.description:
RenderableAppTypes is `app_types` minus the forms this template cannot
actually build. A v2 template declares `agent` for documentation purposes
but carries no canvas, and a v3 pack only instantiates the form it declares
— letting the wizard offer those buttons produces a guaranteed 41105/41104
refusal after the user has already picked datasets (doc/276 §8.3).

payload_schema.description:
PayloadSchema declares which dialect `payload` speaks, so an exported
document is self-describing instead of leaving the reader to sniff for a
`schema` member (a v2 payload has none by design). It is informational on
import: the stored discriminator is still derived from the decoded payload.

signature.description:
Signature is attached on export when this installation has a signing key
configured. Import verifies it for the audit trail but never lets it
change the trust level (doc/276 §8.7).

aggregate.description:
Aggregate is how the per-dataset verdicts fold into the template verdict:
all_required (default) or any_primary.

datasets.description:
Datasets declares each dataset the scenario expects, with the role it
plays and the parse intent it should be created with.

lineage.description:
Lineage marks payloads whose upstream parse semantics are unknown
(doc/276 §7.2 / R28). Templates copied from a pre-2.0 snapshot carry
`legacy_semantics_unknown` and must be re-forked to gain the contract.

requiredCapabilities.description:
RequiredCapabilities must be satisfied before the scenario can be marked
ready; OptionalCapabilities are shown but never block.

definition.description:
Definition is the exact formula, echoed to the UI so the number can be
recomputed by hand (doc/276 §8.6 口径).

knowledge.description:
Knowledge is the optional 2.0 knowledge contract (doc/276 §7.2). It stays
optional so v1/v2 payloads keep round-tripping; when present it is
validated on every write.

answerability.description:
Answerability is the per-turn honesty claim from the knowledge-ops ledger
(doc/301 T12). `nil` means the ledger has no row for this turn — a turn that
predates the claim, or one that never reached the ledger at all. The UI shows
that as "not recorded"; it must never be rendered as "answerable", because a
missing measurement is not a passing measurement.

mode.description:
Mode tells the wizard which half of itself is valid right now: "engine"
means the full application router is serving this request (so the
admin-only step has POST /system/setup/admin), "wizard" means only the
bootstrap router is up and the operator must submit the full form.

idempotency_key.description:
Unified instantiation state machine (doc/276 §7.5 / R24). The idempotency
key comes from the `Idempotency-Key` header only, and the partial unique
index on (tenant_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key <> '' is what
actually makes instantiation idempotent — upstream probing is best-effort.

name_key.description:
NameKey records the requested instance name so instantiation replays can
find the same projection (doc/124 §2.2); it is not the assistant name.

upstream_refs.description:
UpstreamRefs keeps the ids of resources already created in the engine so a
retry can skip them; it is never used to rewrite local state.

budget_policy.description:
BudgetPolicy and AutoConfirmPolicy are optional strings; empty means inherit.
A pointer would also work, but "empty string = inherit" is already the
convention of every other optional string on this surface, and a JSON `null`
and an omitted field would then behave differently for no benefit.

gate_eligible.description: GateEligible is always false and exists only so the UI can state it.

validation_scope.description:
ValidationScope + ApplicationExecutionVerified state the boundary of what
this run proves (doc/276 §7.6 / R6). P0 only runs Knowledge Trials, so the
UI must never render "three forms verified" from a trial run.

conflict_count.description:
ConflictCount and ConflictLabels are R13's P1 addition (doc/288 §9.6「P1 加支持度
与冲突提示」): the previewed sources disagree about the same keyed fact. It is
the same detector the written section uses (`reportEvidenceSignals`), run early
enough that the reviewer can unbind a dataset before paying for the run.

It is *not* a verdict about the section: a conflict found in the preview may
never reach the body (the writer cites what it uses). `0` means "no conflict
among the chunks we looked at", which is not "no conflict in the corpus".

excerpt.description:
Excerpt is the opening of the best-ranked chunk, so the reviewer sees what the
section would be written from instead of only how many hits it has. Truncated
to `reportEvidencePreviewExcerptRunes` and whitespace-collapsed: the dialog is a
preview, and a wrapped 2KB paragraph is not previewable.

insufficient.description:
Insufficient is the only judgement here, and it is nullable: `nil` means the
preview could not be computed, so a client must render "未评估" instead of an
alarm or an all-clear.

note.description:
Note is a machine word (`no_datasets`, `retrieval_unavailable`), not prose: the
UI owns the wording, and a note is the only field that explains a `null`
`insufficient`.

error_code.description:
ErrorCode is the report-family code explaining the reason, when one exists.
Generic section failures have none, and inventing a code would make the
closed set lie.

external_run_id.description:
ExternalRunID is the remote run id for a RAGFlow-backed adapter, kept on
the X run row so operators never have to open the engine to explain a run.

triggered_by.description:
TriggeredBy is the acting user for manual runs and "system" for scheduled
runs, so the run row is self-describing without joining audit logs.

schedule.description:
Schedule accepts either the flat form ("schedule":"interval") or the
doc/225 §7.2 object form ({"kind":"interval","minutes":30}).

grace_hours.description:
GraceHours is how long the retired key keeps working. Omitted = server
default; the service clamps whatever it gets, because an unbounded grace is an
unbounded lifetime for a credential that was supposed to be replaced.

acknowledge_shared_impact.description:
AcknowledgeSharedImpact is required when other applications already use
the dataset.

pushdown_enabled.description:
PushdownEnabled is the local retrieval-pushdown policy (doc/276 §7.4 /
R26): stored on rgx_dataset_link, never pushed to the engine config.

BearerAuth.description: `Authorization: Bearer <credential>` — the JWT from /api/v1/auth/login for the control plane, or a tenant API key for the gateway (`/v1/...`, same header; internal/handler/gateway.go strips the prefix).

post.description: createReport starts one report run. The `Idempotency-Key` header is request identity, not a content fingerprint (doc/288 §7.7): the same key must return the same report and job, a different key must be allowed to ask the same question again. The service owns the validation (44114 for missing/malformed) and the replay, so the handler passes the raw header through and reports whatever the service decided — including `created=false` on a replay, which the UI needs to distinguish from a fresh run. 202, not 200: the aggregate exists but the content does not. Answering 200 would claim a finished report and make the first `GET /reports/:id` look like a regression.。需要权限 execute:report（由 accessRules 强制）。本接口不接受请求体，服务端会忽略请求体内容。成功返回 *service.CreateReportResult

The response is the new sharing view, not 204: the panel must show what the server actually stored (a grantee the server skipped, a policy it normalised) instead of echoing what the client sent.。只要求登录，没有额外的 RBAC 规则。请求体类型 service.SetReportAccessRequest。成功返回 *service.ReportAccessView。声明了 1 个业务错误码：44105(400)（括号内是 HTTP 状态）

post.description: createReportRevision starts one new run on an already-published report. Same conditions, same report: it mints revision `current+1` from the published base and a fresh `report_generate` job in one transaction (doc/288 §7.10). The `Idempotency-Key` header is required (44114) and lives in its OWN namespace — a creation key can never replay here, and a regeneration key can never collide with the key that minted the report (§7.10 "不受创建幂等键拦截"). There is no body: P0-A's "重新生成（同条件）" has nothing a caller may change.。只要求登录，没有额外的 RBAC 规则。请求体类型 service.RegenerateReportRequest。成功返回 *service.CreateReportResult。声明了 1 个业务错误码：44105(400)（括号内是 HTTP 状态）
